drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 defines Foundry as an autonomous computational-systems factory whose purpose is to convert intent into verified running systems and keep actual systems aligned with intended state.
drafts.subject: Foundry

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01's founding thesis states that implementation artifacts are replaceable while the durable asset is the evidence-backed system of intent, decisions, constraints, and verification obligations.
drafts.subject: Foundry

drafts.rationale: Law 1 in EV-T1-01 holds that no artifact is canonical merely because it exists; evidence may support or challenge intent, but existence does not create authority.
drafts.subject: Intended state

drafts.rationale: Law 2 in EV-T1-01 requires Foundry to continuously reason about the delta between authorized intended state and actual state, and that every operation help explain, reduce, verify, or authorize that delta.
drafts.subject: Foundry operations

drafts.rationale: Law 3 in EV-T1-01 forbids any model from being canonical project memory and requires bounded compiled context; EV-T1-02 applies this so addresses and persistent semantic state live outside models.
drafts.subject: Models

drafts.rationale: Law 4 in EV-T1-01 orders executors from deterministic computation up to human authority; EV-T1-02 restates that routing for retrieval, cluster adjudication, high-risk merges, and human escalation.
drafts.subject: Work routing

drafts.rationale: Law 5 in EV-T1-01 separates generation from verification so a creator cannot be sole authority for correctness; EV-T1-02 requires AI judgments to be admitted by Foundry and unresolved judge disagreement to apply no transition.
drafts.subject: Generation

drafts.rationale: Law 6 in EV-T1-01 requires Foundry to treat material ambiguity as a defect, distinguish missing from ambiguous from capability-exceeding decisions, and increase precision only as far as required.
drafts.subject: Intent specifications

drafts.rationale: Law 7 in EV-T1-01 requires every material belief to separate confidence, authority, and provenance; EV-T1-02 places confidence on judgments only and authority on claims.
drafts.subject: Material beliefs

drafts.rationale: Law 8 in EV-T1-01 forbids research from directly mutating canonical intent and requires the Research to Evidence to Reasoning to Authorization to Canonical State flow; EV-T1-02 makes that split structural as judgment-recorded versus transition-applied events.
drafts.subject: Research

drafts.rationale: Law 9 in EV-T1-01 requires every material unknown to be resolved or explicitly controlled; EV-T1-02 keeps disputed claims in durable state and forbids relations from suppressing a DISPUTED issue.
drafts.subject: Material unknowns

drafts.rationale: Law 10 in EV-T1-01 requires append-only history from which current state is reconstructable; EV-T1-02 specifies immutable judgments, versioned issues, and history that references version and judgment IDs only.
drafts.subject: Meaningful changes

drafts.rationale: Law 11 in EV-T1-01 requires Foundry to answer why an artifact exists, what intent requires it, what evidence and verification support it, what depends on it, who authorized it, and whether actual behavior diverges.
drafts.subject: Meaningful artifacts

drafts.rationale: Law 12 in EV-T1-01 requires one universal lifecycle and semantic core across software, infrastructure, data, ML, agents, and future artifacts, with adapters forbidden from creating separate sources of truth.
drafts.subject: Foundry architecture

drafts.rationale: Law 13 in EV-T1-01 locates global understanding in the system representation rather than one model invocation; EV-T1-02 requires bounded cluster inputs and Foundry-owned addresses so no durable object depends on a model's vocabulary.
drafts.subject: Global understanding

drafts.rationale: Law 14 in EV-T1-01 treats creation and operation as the same reconciliation loop at different lifecycle points and forbids splitting development and operations into unrelated control systems.
drafts.subject: Creation and operation

drafts.rationale: Law 15 in EV-T1-01 requires implementations that violate these laws for convenience to change, and requires any falsified law to be amended explicitly with evidence and rationale preserved.
drafts.subject: Foundry Constitution

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 states the design is PROPOSED, awaiting architect review, not approved, not implemented, supersedes nothing, and leaves Intent Intelligence v1 frozen.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 states v1 discovers the right issues then emits them several times under several labels because it lacks durable semantic identity and a governed consolidation stage; measured post-discovery output was +31 predictions with 26 redundant.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v1

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 assigns open-ended meaning questions solely to AI as unapplied SemanticJudgment proposals, and assigns schema checks, admissibility, application, invariants, and retrieval to deterministic Foundry, which may never originate an open-ended semantic conclusion.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 forbids same subject string, GapKind, embedding similarity, shared source event, shared ancestor, or confidence threshold from ever becoming an authoritative semantic rule; such signals may only decide what deserves comparison.
drafts.subject: Semantic identity

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 rejects gap-centric consolidation and semantic-state-first discovery, and recommends Option C: keep v1 discovery framing, adjudicate bindings and relations, consolidate into persistent semantic state, then project gaps with late GapKind.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 makes address identity a Foundry-owned opaque ID; subject, facet, and scope are descriptors never compared for equality, and a candidate reaches an address only through an admitted AI binding.
drafts.subject: SemanticAddress

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 places predicate, structured value, and unit on claims, keeps claims append-only, and forbids merging, rewriting, or averaging claims so conflicting values at one address remain intact.
drafts.subject: SemanticClaim

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 defines consolidation as deterministic application of admitted relations yielding one live issue per address that unions evidence and appends claims; only EQUIVALENT may merge, and it merges addresses never claims.
drafts.subject: Consolidation

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 keeps seven relations and states EQUIVALENT is the only merge-eligible relation; CONFLICTS_WITH relates claims and never merges, while NARROWS, CONSEQUENCE_OF, BUNDLES, OVERLAPS, and DISTINCT do not merge addresses.
drafts.subject: Semantic relations

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 treats conflict as first-class DISPUTED state computed from admitted CONFLICTS_WITH, forbids consolidation from reducing distinct claim values, and allows only an authority event to settle while keeping losing claims readable.
drafts.subject: Semantic conflicts

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 has AI propose BUNDLES with SplitProposal seams; Foundry must enforce that unit evidence edges union-equal the parent set and must not use sentence boundaries as semantic seams.
drafts.subject: Bundled candidates

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 attributes v1's settled-matter reopenings to judging materiality from isolated prose, and requires assess_materiality to see existing canonical decisions, authority, supersession, and closure state; Foundry projects a gap only when genuinely unresolved and materially affecting intent.
drafts.subject: Issue materiality

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 replaces source-ID existence checks with AI entailment verdicts SUPPORTED, PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED, NOT_SUPPORTED, and CONTRADICTED per cited event, and states a valid source ID is never proof of grounding.
drafts.subject: Claim grounding

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 removes GapKind from identity, assigns it after consolidation over the consolidated issue, and treats Gap as a projection from persistent issues rather than a durable object; discovery may emit only an advisory gap_hypothesis.
drafts.subject: Gaps

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 requires correction by append-plus-supersede, never destructive mutation; merges retain contributing candidates and evidence unions so they are reversible, and superseded interpretations remain readable with original inputs.
drafts.subject: Semantic judgments

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 bounds slice 1 to frozen v1 discovery, capped retrieval, bounded cluster adjudication, deterministic consolidation, late classification, and in-memory single-run state, excluding cross-run persistence, supersession machinery, embeddings, and human escalation.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 claims a persistent AI-semantic plus deterministic-governance pipeline can preserve frontier-level critical recall while improving useful precision and lowering redundancy and unsupported rates; it explicitly does not yet claim the lifecycle persistence benefit.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 leaves unresolved the retrieval cap K, whether embeddings earn complexity, whether late classification improves GapKind accuracy, whether discovery kinds should shrink, whether total cost falls, and cross-model address stability, each named with the experiment that would resolve it.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 asks the architect whether per-cycle discovery remains worth performing given identical 9L coverage with a one-shot frontier model, which would shift validation from cleaner single-pass output to the lifecycle experiment rather than changing Option C.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 states Foundry's purpose as converting intent into verified running systems and keeping actual systems aligned with intended state.

value.text: Convert intent into verified running systems and continuously keep actual systems aligned with their intended state.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 founding thesis states implementation artifacts are replaceable while the evidence-backed decision system is the durable asset.

value.text: The durable intellectual asset is the evidence-backed system of intent, decisions, constraints, contracts, invariants, rationale, authority, and verification obligations; Foundry preserves decisions and manufactures replaceable artifacts.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 1 places intended state above artifacts and denies that existence confers authority.

value.text: No artifact is canonical merely because it exists; evidence may support or challenge intent, but existence does not automatically create authority, and a production behavior can be real and still be wrong.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 2 requires continuous reconciliation of intended and actual state via that delta.

value.text: Foundry continuously reasons about Delta = Actual State - Intended State; every operation must help explain, reduce, verify, or explicitly authorize this delta across greenfield, brownfield, features, migrations, incidents, security, infrastructure, ML, and maintenance.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 3 and EV-T1-02 treat models as bounded compute, not durable project memory.

value.text: No model is the canonical memory of a project; persistent state lives outside models, which receive bounded compiled context, transform, return structured results, and may disappear. Context is rent.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 4 and EV-T1-02 §20 require the cheapest trustworthy executor for the needed confidence and risk.

value.text: Work is routed in preferred order: deterministic computation, cheap model worker, stronger model worker, frontier reasoning, then human authority; project size alone must not force a stronger brain.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 5 and EV-T1-02 §4.3/§21 forbid generation from certifying itself.

value.text: The process that creates a proposal or artifact cannot be its sole authority for correctness; generation and verification are separate, and acceptance depends on satisfied obligations rather than the generator's claim of success.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 6 treats ambiguity as a first-class defect rather than assuming written rules are executable.

value.text: Materially ambiguous intent is a first-class defect; Foundry must distinguish a missing decision from an ambiguous decision and from a decision that exceeds a worker's reasoning capability, increasing precision only as far as required.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 7 and EV-T1-02 §8 keep confidence, authority, and provenance independent.

value.text: Every material belief must distinguish confidence (evidential support), authority (whether it may define intended state), and provenance; a highly confident inference is still an inference until authorized as canonical intent.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 8 and EV-T1-02 §18 make research evidence rather than truth and separate recorded judgments from applied transitions.

value.text: Research cannot directly mutate canonical intent. Required flow is Research -> Evidence -> Reasoning -> Authorization -> Canonical State, preserving provenance, disagreement, scope, freshness, and uncertainty.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 9 and EV-T1-02 §13/§17 forbid material unknowns disappearing silently.

value.text: Every material unknown must be resolved or explicitly controlled; a known bounded non-blocking uncertainty may travel with the system, but an uncontrolled material unknown must block affected downstream work.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 10 and EV-T1-02 §18 require reconstructable append-only history of judgments and transitions.

value.text: Foundry maintains an append-only history of material events, claims, evidence, decisions, amendments, verification outcomes, and promotions so current state is reconstructable and the system can answer how and why it became true.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 11 lists those explainability obligations for meaningful artifacts and behaviors.

value.text: For every meaningful artifact or behavior Foundry should answer why it exists, what intent requires it, what evidence supports it, what verifies it, what depends on it, what change would affect, who authorized it, how it changed, and whether actual behavior diverges; unexplained meaningful artifacts are technical debt.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 12 requires one kernel across domains rather than separate products or truths.

value.text: One universal lifecycle and semantic core across software, infrastructure, data, ML, agents, models, prompts, and future computational artifacts; domain adapters must not create separate sources of truth. Greenfield and brownfield are different initial conditions of the same architecture.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 13 and EV-T1-02 §3/§10 locate global understanding in system state, not one model context.

value.text: Global understanding belongs to the system representation, not to a single model invocation; Foundry scales by decomposition, persistent state, and compiled context rather than one brain holding the whole project.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 14 unifies build and operate as one reconciliation loop.

value.text: Creation and operation are the same reconciliation loop at different lifecycle points; before deployment Foundry closes intent versus missing artifacts, after deployment intended versus observed reality, and must not split development and operations into unrelated control systems.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 15 gives the constitution precedence over implementation convenience.

value.text: If a proposed implementation violates these laws for convenience, the implementation must change; if experiments falsify a law, the law must be amended explicitly with evidence and rationale preserved. Nothing is sacred except what survives evidence.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 Status states the v2 design is proposed, awaiting architect review, not approved, and not implemented.

value.text: PROPOSED — awaiting architect review; not approved; not implemented

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §1–§2 identify the v1 defect as missing semantic identity and consolidation after discovery, with those frozen measurements.

value.text: v1 discovers the right unresolved issues then emits each several times under several labels with no durable semantic identity or governed consolidation; measured +31 predictions equal -1 useful, +6 unsupported, +26 redundant, and 0 of 44 duplicate pairs share GapKind.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §4.3 states this AI-versus-Foundry responsibility boundary as the governing rule.

value.text: AI may propose a state-changing semantic judgment but may never apply one; deterministic Foundry may apply or refuse a state transition but may never originate an open-ended semantic conclusion.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §4.4 lists those forbidden authoritative shortcuts and confines them to candidate retrieval.

value.text: Same subject string, same GapKind, high embedding similarity, shared source event, shared semantic ancestor, and AI confidence above a threshold must never be authoritative semantic identity rules; each may be used only to decide that candidates deserve comparison.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §5 rejects Options A and B and §6 recommends Option C as the v2 architecture.

value.text: Option C — hybrid: semantic candidate → governed state → gap projection

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §7.2 defines SemanticAddress identity as the opaque ID with descriptors that are not keys.

value.text: Identity is a Foundry-owned opaque stable address_id; subject, facet, and scope are AI-normalized descriptors never compared for equality as keys, and a candidate reaches an address only through an admitted AI binding judgment.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §7.1 and §7.3 place predicate/value/unit on claims and prohibit merging claims.

value.text: A SemanticClaim binds predicate plus structured value (quantity, enumeration, text, or UNDECIDED) and unit only for quantity, with at least one evidence edge; claims are append-only and are never merged, rewritten, or averaged.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §3, §12, and decision 6 define consolidation as merging addresses only, never claims.

value.text: Consolidation is deterministic application of admitted AI relations yielding one live issue per address by merging addresses, appending claims, and unioning evidence; claims are never merged or reconciled, making silent conflict destruction structurally impossible.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §9 enumerates these relations and states EQUIVALENT is the only merge-eligible relation.

value.text: Seven relations: EQUIVALENT (only merge-eligible, merges addresses), NARROWS, CONSEQUENCE_OF, BUNDLES (triggers split, never merges), CONFLICTS_WITH (relates claims, never merges), OVERLAPS, and DISTINCT.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §8, §13, and invariant 4 require conflicts to become DISPUTED rather than collapse.

value.text: A conflict is first-class state: admitted CONFLICTS_WITH at an address sets DISPUTED; no transition may clear DISPUTED except an authority event that settles the address; losing claims are SUPERSEDED and remain readable; a merge that would reduce distinct claim values is refused.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §14 requires evidence-union equality on splits and forbids using sentence boundaries as seams.

value.text: BUNDLES never merges; AI returns a SplitProposal whose units re-enter retrieval. The union of unit evidence edges must equal the parent candidate's evidence set or the split is refused; sentence and clause boundaries are never semantic seams.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §15 specifies those compiled inputs and the deterministic projection gate over the AI judgment.

value.text: assess_materiality receives the issue, claims, and evidence plus existing canonical decisions at or near the address, relevant authority records, supersession history, and current scope and closure state; policy projects a gap only when genuinely_unresolved AND materially_affects_intent.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §16 keeps those four entailment verdicts, cuts INSUFFICIENT, and denies that a valid source ID proves grounding.

value.text: SUPPORTED; PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED; NOT_SUPPORTED; CONTRADICTED (INSUFFICIENT cut)

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §3, §17, and decision 12–13 make gaps projected views with late GapKind assignment.

value.text: Gap is a projection, not the durable object; GapKind is removed from identity and assigned by AI after consolidation over the consolidated issue. Discovery may emit only an advisory non-binding gap_hypothesis. DISPUTED issues cannot be suppressed by a relation.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §19 defines append-and-supersede correction and requires merge reversibility.

value.text: Correction is always append plus supersede, never destructive mutation; judgments remain readable with original inputs, every merge is reversible via contributing candidates and evidence union, and affected projections are recomputed.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §23 states this primary testable claim and withholds the future lifecycle claim.

value.text: A persistent AI-semantic plus deterministic-governance pipeline can preserve frontier-level critical intent coverage while producing cleaner, better-grounded, less redundant unresolved semantic state than one-shot frontier analysis on the same evidence (non-inferior critical recall; strictly better useful precision, redundancy, and unsupported rate; serious safety violations <= baseline). The lifecycle persistence claim is explicitly not yet to be asserted.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §25 and decision 17 define this smallest independently falsifiable v2 slice and its exclusions.

value.text: Slice 1: frozen v1 discovery, deterministic retrieval, bounded AI cluster adjudication, deterministic consolidation, late classification and gap projection; in-memory single-run addresses and issues with full invariants. Not in slice 1: cross-run persistence, event-store integration, supersession machinery, embedding retrieval, materiality-from-canonical-decisions, or human escalation.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §27 deferred-decisions table names these items and the experiments that resolve them.

value.text: Deferred pending named experiments: candidate cap K and retrieval-signal mix; whether embedding retrieval earns its complexity; whether late classification improves GapKind accuracy; whether the 11 discovery semantic kinds should shrink; whether total v2 cost falls below v1; cross-model/cross-provider address stability.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §27 open architecture question leaves the validating experiment blocked on whether discovery is commodity.

value.text: 9L showed a one-shot frontier model matching Foundry semantic coverage exactly. If the architect treats discovery as commodity, recommended architecture is unchanged but v2 validation should shift from cleaner single-pass output to the §25 lifecycle experiment. Blocked: which experiment v2 must pass to be considered validated.
